title: Computer Keyboard Finger Placement Game
problem: First-time students in our school lab type with just one finger while looking at the keys, taking 5 minutes to type one sentence.
idea: A typing game where a sprite moves only when you press the right home-row key. Here, test yourself: which finger presses which key?

questions.why: Left hand rests on A S D F. F is the index finger. It has a small bump!
Right hand rests on J K L ;. J has a bump too.
The little finger rests on A.
J = index, K = middle, L = ring, ; = little finger.

widgets.heading: ✅ Good typing habits
widgets.intro: Tick what you did in today's lab class.

items.text: Fingers resting on A S D F and J K L ;
Felt the bumps on F and J without looking
items.te: చూడకుండా F, J మీద గుర్తులు తాకాను

items.text: Sat straight with the screen at eye level
Looked at the screen, not the keys

bands.text: Typing star! Speed will come with practice. ⌨️
Good. Keep your eyes on the screen.
Start with the home row today. Slow is okay!

how: Ask Gemini to explain home-row finger placement in simple steps.
In Scratch, make a sprite and a 'target key' that shows a random letter from A S D F J K L.
Use 'when key pressed' blocks: if it matches the target, move the sprite forward and add 1 to score.
If the wrong key is pressed, play a soft sound and show the right finger.
Add a 60-second timer and show the score at the end.
Let lab students play it before each typing class.
prompt: I am a Class 8 student making a Scratch typing game. Explain the home-row finger placement on a keyboard in 5 simple steps, and give me 10 easy practice words using only A S D F J K L keys.
